 Oral Judgment
1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) has been filed by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 31.05.2019 passed by the MACT, Mangaluru D.K. in MVC No.545/2016.
2.

Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 24.01.2016, the deceased Padmanabha Shetty had crossed half of the road of four lane and was NC: 2024:KHC:37688 waiting to cross the road on divider, opposite Karmbisthana Temple, Jeppinamogaru, Mangaluru in order to go to Udupi at about 7.00 p.m., at that time, a rider of motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-19/EH-1595 rode that vehicle in a high speed, rash and negligent manner from Thokkattu side by overtaking another vehicle and hit to the deceased.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondent No.2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.

The respondent No.1, despite service Smt. Susheela Shetty vs Mr. Arun Kumar K on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87413611/
2 of notice, did not appear before the Tribunal and was placed ex-parte.

sentences.text:
On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the claim petition and held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.8,36,577/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, this appeal has been filed.

6. The learned counsel for the claimants has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, the claimants assert that the deceased was aged about 48 years at the time of the accident and had an income of Rs.800/- per day as a Meson and to prove the same, they produced Ex.P11-Salary Certificate and examined employer of the deceased as PW-2.

However, the assessment of income of the deceased at Rs.7,500/-
by the Tribunal is unjustified and erroneous.
NC: 2024:KHC:37688 b) Secondly, at the time of the accident, the deceased was aged about 48 years, as evidenced by Ex.P5-Wound Certificate and Ex.P6-Postmortem Report.
However, the Tribunal erroneously considered the deceased's age to be between 51-55 years and applied a multiplier of '11', which is inconsistent with the documentary evidence on record.
c) Thirdly, since there are four dependents, it would be appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards 'personal expenses.
However, The Tribunal has erred in deducting 1/3rd of the income of the deceased towards 'personal expenses'.

d) Fourthly, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -V- NANU RAM [2018 ACJ 2782], each of the claimants is entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of love and affection and consortium'.
NC: 2024:KHC:37688 e) Lastly, considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is inadequate and on the lower side.

7. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised the following counter- contentions:

sentences.text:
a) Firstly, although the claimants claim that the deceased was earning Rs.800/- per day and examined his employer, the employer did not produce any Income Tax Returns to show that he was paying a salary of Rs.800/-
per day to his employers.
Consequently, the Tribunal has correctly assessed the income of the deceased notionally.
b) Secondly, the age of the deceased is mentioned in Ex.P10-Copy of the Ration Card as 49 years in the year 2015 and the accident occurred in the year 2016.
Considering the same, the Tribunal correctly applied the multiplier for the age group of 51-55 years, which is '11'.
c) Thirdly, on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence and considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

With the above contentions, the learned counsel sought to dismiss the appeal.
8.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
9. It is not in dispute that Padmanabha Shetty died on 12.06.2016 in the road traffic accident occurred on 24.01.2016 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.

10. The specific case of the claimants that the deceased was earning Rs.800/- per day and to prove the same, they produced Salary Certificate and examined the employer of NC: 2024:KHC:37688 the deceased as PW-2.
Considering the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2, since the deceased was working as a mason, the monthly income of the deceased can be assessed at Rs.10,000/-.
To the aforesaid income, 25% has to be added on account of future prospects in view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in 'PRANAY SETHI' (supra).
Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.12,500/-.
Since there are four dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards personal expenses and remaining amount has to be taken as his contribution to the family.
The further case of the claimants that the deceased was aged about 48 years at the time of the accident.
The age of the deceased is mentioned in Ex.P10-Copy of the Ration Card as 49 years in the year 2015 and the accident occurred in the year 2016.
Therefore, the age of the deceased has to be considered as 50 years as on the date of the accident.
Thus, the multiplier applicable to his age group is '13'.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to NC: 2024:KHC:37688 compensation of Rs.14,62,500/- (Rs.12,500*12*13*3/4) on account of 'loss of dependency'.
11.
In addition, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'loss of estate' and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'funeral expenses'.
Claimant No.1, wife of the deceased is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of spousal consortium'.

12. In view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of 'MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE' (supra), claimant Nos.2 and 3, children of the deceased are entitled for compensation Smt. Susheela Shetty vs Mr. Arun Kumar K on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87413611/
4 of Rs.40,000/- each under the head of 'loss of parental consortium' and claimant No.4, mother of the deceased is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of filial consortium'.
13.

The compensation of Rs.1,06,577/- awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'medical expenses' is based on - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:37688 the medical bills produced by the claimants and is deemed just and reasonable.
14.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to the following compensation:
 Compensation under Amount in  different Heads (Rs.)
 Loss of dependency 14,62,500  Funeral expenses 15,000  Loss of estate 15,000  Loss of spousal consortium 40,000  Loss of Parental consortium 80,000  Loss of Filial consortium 40,000  Medical Expenses 1,06,577

In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
